answer_to_band_question.llm_data_read: The immediate LLM-data need is not proven to be one rank band. The stronger finding is that we should add denser, programmatic frequency metadata and then test whether very-common trigger abstention persists before using a top-N difficulty formula confidently.
answer_to_band_question.main_read: The representative-proxy lane does not prove that bands perform the same. It shows low positive allow across most source-rank bands, while the denser Zipf fallback suggests very common triggers may be especially abstain-heavy. That is a promising clue, not yet a stable curve.
answer_to_band_question.product_read: Current browser-like behavior is conservative: negative rows are all abstained, while positive allow is 24.5%. That is safer than over-replacing, but it misses many good replacements.

methodology.primary_question: Within the filled representative-proxy lane, do frequency or heuristic bands explain current allow/abstain behavior?
methodology.promotion_rule: This report is diagnostic only. It cannot promote a formula because the representative lane still has sparse source-rank coverage and agent-draft rows that need review.

next_steps: Use this report to separate real product behavior from old authored stress-lane behavior.
Improve metadata coverage for the representative lane before claiming a beginner/intermediate/advanced curve.
Rerun formula and threshold bakeoffs on representative case traces, but keep source-rank-known and source-rank-missing rows separate.
Add observed browser contexts or reviewed LLM rows where representative bands are sparse or metadata-missing.

sample_warnings.message: 87 of 120 representative rows lack source-rank metadata, so frequency-band curves are still fragile.
Some source_rank cells have fewer than 10 cases: 1-500, 501-1000, >5000. Treat their rates as directional only.
